text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging oncall: HERMES-VPC isolation detected in dedicated pool 'dp-west-3'. Tenant hermes-corp (tenant_id=hermes-84) showing KV cache thrash and ~20% packet drops to inference nodes. Impact: 10-20% of requests 5xx / long tail latency. Investigating now.

Maya (oncall): I'm on it. @Theo can you grab network & infra logs for dp-west-3? starting triage.

Theo (sre): pulling logs. seeing repeated connection timeouts from node g-12 and g-13 to the router. kernel drops spike at 14:03 UTC. sharing pcap + ifconfig output in case channel.

Priya (CS): Heads up — Hermes support flagged customer-facing errors at 14:05 — they have active ramp in APAC. I'm joining the call in 2.

Eddie (support): Hermes says their routed requests to /v1/generate are getting 504s and 'no available worker' errors. They attempted retry logic and saw duplicate tokens charged. Need customer impact window for comms.

Maya (oncall): quick mitigation idea: move hermes-corp traffic to cold fallback region (dp-east-1) with routing policy 'dedicated-failover' plus temporary capacity burst. Can we do a safe redirect w/ sticky session drain? @Clarisse

Clarisse (eng-runtime): We can route at the smart-router layer. Two options:
1) soft-route: TCP-level redirect -> may drop in-flight KV cache (slower) but quick.
2) cold-spot: spin up ephemeral worker in dp-east-1 and do traffic cutover via policy. preserves session token mapping if we warm KV cache with prefixes.

Theo (sre): spinning ephemeral workers takes ~90s to register. kernel issue seems localized to g-12/g-13; could cordon and re-route only hermes-corp.

Maya (oncall): Execute plan B: cordon g-12/g-13 from pool, enable 'dedicated-failover' for tenant hermes-84 to dp-east-1, warm caches with last-5-min prefetched prompts, then verify 200s. I will run commands.

ops-bot: command issued by Maya: "rbac cordon-node g-12 ; rbac cordon-node g-13 ; routing set-policy hermes-84 dedicated-failover dp-east-1 ; warm-cache hermes-84 --prefetch 5m"

Maya (oncall): cordon done. routing policy applied. warming caches now (k=50 concurrent prefetch). ETA 45s.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Cache warming completed for tenant hermes-84. New worker pool registered in dp-east-1 (ephemeral-hera-1..3). Monitoring.

Eddie (support): Hermes engineering confirms traffic is now flowing, rates normalizing. They still see occasional 502s but majority 200. I'm drafting a status message.

Priya (CS): Great — customers in the account slack say reduced errors. I told them we're doing controlled reroute and will follow up with RCA and credits. @Jules please prepare exec note.

Jules (acct exec): On it. We'll prepare a short exec summary (timeline, impact, mitigation, credits) and loop in legal for wording re: SLA. How long was the impact window? Need exact times.

Maya (oncall): Root window: 14:02 UTC (first drops) -> 14:13 UTC (majority routed to dp-east-1). Residual tail 14:13 -> 14:25 UTC with intermittent 502s. I'll capture exact per-route metrics and put in the postmortem.

Clarisse (eng-runtime): Quick note: cordoned nodes show repeated kernel-level RX ring overflow and NIC firmware reports 'link flapping' on g-12. Raising a ticket with infra for hardware replacement. This looks like localized NIC/firmware regression.

Theo (sre): I'll isolate hardware. Marking g-12/g-13 unhealthy and draining. Also enabling stricter circuit-breaker for tenant-level connection retries to avoid duplicate billing.

incident-bot: :pager: Handoff scheduled to day oncall @Theo at 14:30 UTC. Please update the incident lead field.

Theo (sre): Taking lead. Next steps: - confirm hardware replacement schedule; - run KB for NIC firmware rollback on similar nodes; - confirm no cross-tenant impact; - coordinate RCA draft.

Maya (oncall): Logs and dump attached: ```
# sample log snippet
2026-03-15T14:03:22Z worker g-12 ERROR connection timeout to router/10.32.4.1
2026-03-15T14:03:23Z kernel g-12 WARN rx_ring_overflow
``` 

Priya (CS): Hermes wants a consolidated comms timeline and an ask for 10% credit on this month’s bill. Documenting the ask. Also product wants to know if any data exfil happened — confirm no logs left customer data.

Clarisse (eng-runtime): Confirming: it's a networking/hardware level issue affecting packet delivery; inference payloads not persisted outside ephemeral KV cache; no evidence of leaked payloads. Will include in RCA.

Eddie (support): Hermes received duplicate token charges for ~1200 requests due to retry loop. Finance note: calculate gross overcharge and propose credit value. @Jules can help with customer account credits policy.

Jules (acct exec): We usually offer proportional credits for SLA breaches + make-good credits for duplicates. I'll draft 15% of that day's usage and an additional one-time $X make-good. Will run it by legal.

Theo (sre): For postmortem: suspected root cause = NIC firmware regression causing RX ring overflow -> packet drops -> router timeouts -> worker pool thrash. Action items: replace NICs g-12/g-13, push firmware pin for fleet, add saturating alerts on rx_ring_*/kernel-drops, improve routing fallback for dedicated pools to avoid charging duplicates.

Maya (oncall): Adding immediate action: change retry policy for 502/504 to 2 retries with exponential backoff on tenant-level merges. Reducing duplicate charges window.

incident-bot: :lock: Incident sev: P2. Impact: Hermes enterprise (dedicated VPC) partial degradation for ~23 minutes for a subset of requests. Customers notified via CS.

Priya (CS): Draft status to Hermes:
"We detected an infrastructure issue in the dedicated GPU pool affecting a subset of your requests between 14:02–14:25 UTC. We mitigated by routing your traffic to an alternate region and are performing a full RCA. We will issue a credit for the impacted period and follow up with details and preventative steps."

Eddie (support): Hermes accepted preliminary message and asked for ETA on RCA. Can we commit to 72 hours? Typical for hardware RCA + ticketing.

Theo (sre): 72 hours OK. I'll own RCA draft and include logs, timelines, and action items. @Clarisse will add runtime mitigation & config changes. @Maya please attach raw logs and pcap.

Clarisse (eng-runtime): I'll include the code diff for the routing policy change and the retry cap. snippet:
```
route_policy "dedicated-failover" {
  max_retries = 2
  backoff_ms = [100, 400]
  failover_regions = ["dp-east-1"]
}
```

Maya (oncall): Uploading logs + pcap to the incident artifact bucket: s3://redwood-incidents/1882334455/hermes/ (link)

Jules (acct exec): Exec note draft:
- Impacted customer: Hermes (enterprise)
- Window: 14:02–14:25 UTC
- Mitigation: rerouted traffic to dp-east-1, warmed caches, drained faulty nodes
- Next steps: RCA within 72h, credits to be issued, hardware replacements scheduled
I'll iterate and send by EOD.

Priya (CS): After RCA, we'll do a dedicated customer follow-up call with engineering + account exec. Schedule tentatively for tomorrow EOD.

Theo (sre): Adding action items to tracking board:
- HW ticket: replace g-12/g-13 (owner: infra)
- Fleet firmware pin rollout (owner: eng-infra)
- Add rx_ring alert (owner: eng-sre)
- Retry policy update (owner: eng-runtime)
- RCA draft (owner: Theo)

Maya (oncall): Closing immediate page. If anything regresses ping me. Thanks all.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Incident 1882334455 marked 'mitigated'. Handoff complete. Follow-up tasks added to tracker #INC-2026-921.
